clue.text: Bad light obscures one unknown character on a set of steps

indicators.note: to obscure something is to cover it up, so the gloomy word wraps round what follows

blocks.note: murk is gloomy, poor light
one as the article a
z is a standard algebraic unknown
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in dim light can barely make out a strange figure standing on a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: MURK takes in A and Z, then 'on a' adds a final A to give MAZURKA. 'Set of steps' looks like a staircase but means a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A mazurka is a lively Polish dance, and a dance is a sequence of steps in the choreographic sense.

clue.text: State needing, say, Andy Murray's charm

blocks.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state
the tennis player Andy Murray is an example of a Scot; 'say' signals the example

explanation.surface: A nation needs the charm of the tennis star Andy Murray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Andy Murray's charm' reads as his personality, but the possessive just joins him to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, an object or figure kept to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Top religious school badly hit

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism
the letters of hit rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading religious school has been hard hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the highest point, so it serves as a noun for the top or peak of something.

clue.text: Bloody American banknotes that might be pickled!

blocks.note: blood is red
cabbage is American slang for paper money

explanation.surface: Wretched US dollars, the kind that a drunk might squander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickled' hints at drunkenness next to money, but the definition is literal: red cabbage is commonly pickled.
explanation.definitionFit: Red cabbage is a vegetable often preserved in vinegar, so it is a thing that might be pickled.

clue.text: Jelly-like image

blocks.note: as in the sense of like
pic is short for picture

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Jelly-like' glues the definition to the wordplay; split it and 'like' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set or glaze food.

clue.text: Old type of slate roofing in progress – can't leak!

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning their letters

blocks.note: letters running across the end of progress, can't and the start of leak

explanation.surface: Roofers are midway through a job on old slates and the roof had better be watertight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scantle was a gauge, and hence a size of slate, used in traditional roofing; the word is now obsolete.

clue.text: English short of oriental coins at first? Ridiculous!

blocks.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries
standard abbreviation
less meaning without, lacking

explanation.surface: Is England short of Eastern currency? What nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' puts the coins at the front, before 'English short of', read as E-LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless means lacking sense, foolish or absurd, which matches ridiculous as an adjective.

clue.text: Unsubstantial hob lacking force

indicators.note: lacking says something is missing, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a kind of household sprite
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A cooking hob that has lost its power is not much use.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob looks like a stove top here, but it is the old word for a sprite or goblin; lose its F and the answer remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy can mean flimsy or lacking substance, as in airy promises, so it fits unsubstantial.

clue.text: Tree of south-western river in Germany

blocks.note: the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall in south-west England
taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A tree of a south-western river, located somewhere in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree whose pods yield a sour pulp used in cooking.

clue.text: Hence no top and bottom on Brown's hamper

indicators.note: with neither top nor bottom the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: the word hence without its first and last letters
umber is a brown earth pigment, hence a brown colour

explanation.surface: So, without a lid or base, the picnic hamper belongs to Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket, but it is the verb meaning to impede.
explanation.definitionFit: To encumber is to weigh down or impede, the same verb sense as hamper.

clue.text: Council rejected gatherings around New York

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way
around means surrounding, so the gatherings enclose the city

blocks.note: dos are parties or social gatherings
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A council turns down events held in the New York area.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church officials, a kind of governing council.

clue.text: Vessel at Cairo museum's entrance, unusually broad

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so only the opening letter of the word is used
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of museum

explanation.surface: A pot displayed at the entrance to a Cairo museum is remarkably wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Panoramic means giving a wide, sweeping view, so broad in the sense of wide-ranging.

clue.text: Fire-starter, exposed all round gets beaten

indicators.note: all round means encircling, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to be outed is to be exposed publicly
a match starts a fire

explanation.surface: An arsonist, unmasked on every side, is given a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outmatched is to be outclassed by a stronger opponent, so defeated or beaten.

clue.text: A spirit flower

blocks.note: taken as written
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit flower' sounds like a ghostly bloom, but it is two pieces and a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant such as the arum lily, grown for its showy flowering spathe.

clue.text: Defiled Lars' unfinished picture of biblical content?

indicators.note: unfinished means the end is missing, so the last letter is dropped
defiled means spoilt or corrupted, so the letters are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
picture lacking its final letter

explanation.surface: Lars has spoilt his half-done painting of a Bible scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Scriptural means relating to scripture, the Bible, so it describes biblical subject matter; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: See 27
Fittipaldi's bottom pushed into hot rod in ground, swiftish?

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter
pushed into means inserted among other letters
ground as in milled, so the letters are crushed and remixed

blocks.note: the last letter of Fittipaldi
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The racing driver Emerson Fittipaldi is shoved into a hot rod on the track: is he quick enough?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiftish?' does not mean fairly fast: a swift is a bird, and the answer means bird-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornithoid means resembling a bird, and a swift is a bird, so swiftish is a playful example.

clue.text: Part of stage scenery support covering sink

blocks.note: to back is to support
to drop is to sink

explanation.surface: Stagehands put supports around the sink on a set.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'covering' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdrop is a painted cloth hung at the back of a stage as part of the scenery.

clue.text: Compound of element one put into replacement battery

indicators.note: put into means inserted among the other letters
a replacement is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical compound of an element is fitted into a new battery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ytterbia is ytterbium oxide, a chemical compound of the rare-earth element ytterbium.

clue.text: Not against being free, independent, cold and hostile?

indicators.note: letters set free are no longer held in their order and can be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words rearranged
standard abbreviation
C for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone who isn't opposed to freedom and stays independent and aloof: are they hostile?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a nice irony: the fodder says 'not against' while the answer means opposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonistic means actively opposed or unfriendly, the adjective for an adversary.

clue.text: Locks securing army officer, daily

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one word grips the other inside it

blocks.note: a mop is a shock of hair
RSM is a regimental sergeant major

explanation.surface: Hair-locks hold an army officer in place every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaner who comes in each day, and Mrs Mop is the jokey name for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Mop is a humorous British name for a cleaning woman, and a daily is a domestic cleaner.

clue.text: Raised edge of dish, say, turned over

indicators.note: something turned over in a down clue is flipped, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a flan is an open tart
e.g. means for example

explanation.surface: The rim of a dish, for example, has been flipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is a projecting rim or collar on a pipe or wheel, a raised edge for strength or attachment.

clue.text: Artist gets national emblem back to front

indicators.note: back to front here means the back letter goes to the front, leaving the rest in place

blocks.note: the leek is a national emblem of Wales

explanation.surface: A painter receives a country's symbol the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' would usually reverse the word, but here only the last letter moves to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter famous for colourful abstract work.

clue.text: Rural cuts affected outside temperature of a building

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are changed in order
outside means the rearranged letters sit around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Cuts to rural budgets have changed the heating of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Structural means relating to the framework of a building, the parts that hold it up.

clue.text: Henry Kissinger's other bovine feature?

indicators.note: Kissinger had a strong German accent, so the word is as he would pronounce it

blocks.note: other as said in a heavy German accent, with a d sound for the th

explanation.surface: A spoof question about the US statesman's other cow-like trait.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Kissinger, the US statesman, kept a heavy German accent all his life.
explanation.definitionFit: An udder is the milk-producing organ of a cow, so a feature of bovine anatomy.

clue.text: Presently it could be a conspiracy theory – no question

indicators.note: no here means without, so a letter is dropped

blocks.clueFragment: it could be a conspiracy theory
blocks.note: QAnon is a US conspiracy-theory movement
Q is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Soon this might be a conspiracy theory, no doubt about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon or shortly, the archaic sense of presently.

clue.text: Nick, trendy gangster and outlaw

blocks.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
in means fashionable
hood is short for hoodlum

explanation.surface: Nick, a fashionable gangster, and a criminal on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest who robbed the rich.

clue.text: Hit English name for Japanese dish

blocks.note: to ram is to strike hard
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A popular English name given to a Japanese dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as an adjective for a popular name, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramen is a Japanese noodle soup, a dish of wheat noodles in broth.

clue.text: Life-limiting commercial policy of Republican politician harbouring colossal need (NB perverted)

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are distorted
harbouring means sheltering inside, so the politician wraps round the rest

blocks.note: Mike Pence, Republican US vice-president 2017-21
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Republican politician's greed drives a business policy that shortens a product's life.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Pence was the Republican US vice-president from 2017 to 2021; his surname is split around the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned obsolescence is designing goods to wear out or date quickly so that buyers must replace them.

clue.text: Right, go on – backslide!

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
time that goes on elapses

explanation.surface: An encouraging 'all right, go ahead' to someone tempted to lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into an earlier bad state or habit, the verb backslide.
